gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 9 build step is the narrowest honest place to keep the runtime survey family machine-checkable without inventing a runtime loader implementation.

A dedicated survey gate keeps the mixed Phase 6 schedule wording, the real Phase 9 roadmap target, the landed shared runtime-loader seam, the new shared command_name field, and the still-absent argv or environment controls explicit on current master.

The repo already had runtime starter samples, three loader-plan files, and one sample-only blocked trace-events pilot, but it still lacked one shared note that says Phase 6 should not absorb runtime allocator or init-flow work.

The live shared runtime-loader packet already includes atomic64, bitmap, and kretprobe loader plans plus the common `zigux/kernel/runtime_loader.zig` request surface, so one shared substrate-plan note should keep that loader-stage vocabulary and the explicit `waiting_on_runtime_substrate` to `released_without_substrate` fallback aligned instead of leaving it implicit. It also keeps the first shared-request trio explicit while `samples/zigux/runtime_trace_events_loader.zig` stays adjacent to that union as a sample-only blocked scaffold under the separate trace-core freeze boundary.

The bounded runtime-loader starter still needs explicit review cues for hidden runtime services, implicit allocation posture, panic behavior, and visible unsafe ownership while the shared request surface remains pre-execution.

The shared manifest now records the current pre-execution lifecycle boundary directly: `zigux/kernel/runtime_loader.zig` keeps `RuntimeLoadRequest.keepsPreExecutionLifecycleBoundaryExplicit` as the common guard, the three landed sample-side loader plans keep staged init and exit symbols review-only, the kretprobe lane keeps `register_kretprobe` plus `unregister_kretprobe` metadata-only, and no live `module_init()`, `module_exit()`, `register_kretprobe()`, or `unregister_kretprobe()` path is claimed anywhere in this packet.

The atomic64, bitmap, and kretprobe starter lanes now publish staged init and exit symbol names, requires_runtime_substrate flags, selftest-hook markers, and handoff-stage checks, while the kretprobe loader also keeps `register_kretprobe` and `unregister_kretprobe` as metadata-only registration labels that a future shared runtime loader must consume without implying a live registration path.

Each landed sample-side loader already carries an explicit without-substrate rollback path that releases the shared request from waiting_on_runtime_substrate to released_without_substrate, so the validation packet should catalog that fallback posture instead of leaving it implicit in loader-local tests.

The fourth Phase 9 runtime pilot is still `samples/zigux/runtime_trace_events.zig`, and its bounded `samples/zigux/runtime_trace_events_loader.zig` scaffold now exists, but that scaffold remains intentionally outside the first shared-request union because the trace-events packet keeps `kernel/trace/ring_buffer.c` at a study-only boundary and still blocks runtime task ownership, polling and event-loop substrate, thread creation, and tracepoint-registration lifecycle wiring.

The shared runtime-loader blocker now sits adjacent to the freeze map's study-only `kernel/workqueue.c` anchor, so task scheduling, polling, event-loop behavior, and any workqueue-parity status change must stay blocked until the Architecture Council reopens that boundary with fresh evidence.

The roadmap's first command and environment plumbing surfaces live in Phase 8 tooling, with the live repo now landing `tools/lib/subcmd/exec-cmd.zig` and `tools/lib/subcmd/help.zig` around `ExtractArgv0Result.command_name`, `Config.exec_path_env`, `PERF_EXEC_PATH`, `PATH`, `LINES`, and `COLUMNS`, and the shared runtime loader now carries a shared command_name field, but argv-policy and environment-derived activation handling still remain blocked.

The shared runtime-loader request surface now consumes the allocator policy contract directly, so allocator ownership, fallback rules, and init-flow posture are machine-checkable before any real runtime loader behavior exists.

The shared runtime-loader request surface now carries staged entry and exit symbol names from all three landed sample-side loader plans, and the kretprobe lane keeps `register_kretprobe` plus `unregister_kretprobe` as metadata-only registration labels, so the common lifecycle contract is explicit even though no real runtime execution or registration path exists.
